message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to very different lineages: lions are felids in the order **Carnivora**, while zebras are equids in the order **Perissodactyla** (odd‑toed ungulates).  

Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders, which lies deep in the mammalian tree.  In modern phylogenetic terms this ancestor is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria** (the group that includes Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, and Eulipotyphla).  That ancestor lived roughly **90–100 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous, long before the split that produced the distinct carnivore and odd‑toed ungulate lineages.

In short, the common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is a very ancient placental mammal that existed about 90–100 million years ago, predating the divergence of the major mammalian orders that give rise to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.

So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But maybe the question expects "the common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all mammals, which lived about 160 million years ago." That ancestor would have lived around 70-80 million years ago? Actually the divergence between Carnivora and Perissodactyla is older, maybe around 100 million years ago. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is older, around 160-200 million years ago. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 160 million years ago. Or we could say "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla, which existed around 70-80 million years ago." Let's check: The divergence of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is part of the Laurasiatheria clade. The last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which is older than 70 million years. According to some sources, the divergence of Laurasiatheria from other placental mammals occurred around 90-100 million years ago. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which is about 90-100 million years ago.
